USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

Indication after blunt trauma

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 43-year-old is assessed after a motor vehicle collision. He is alert but has midline cervical tenderness and tingling in both hands. Blood pressure and breathing are stable. Which approach to spinal motion is most appropriate during the initial evaluation?

  1. Ask the patient to forcefully rotate his neck to prove stability
  2. Use the absence of hypotension to exclude spine injury
  3. Restrict only the painful wrist and ignore the neck
  4. Restrict unnecessary spinal movement while assessing for injury
  5. Clear the cervical spine because the patient is awake
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Restrict unnecessary spinal movement while assessing for injury

Midline tenderness and neurologic symptoms justify precautions and further evaluation despite preserved alertness.

Understanding the options

Restrict unnecessary spinal movement while assessing for injury
Midline tenderness and neurologic symptoms justify precautions and further evaluation despite preserved alertness.
Clear the cervical spine because the patient is awake
Alertness alone does not negate pain or neurologic findings.
Ask the patient to forcefully rotate his neck to prove stability
Provocative movement is inappropriate with these concerning findings.
Use the absence of hypotension to exclude spine injury
Hemodynamic stability does not establish spinal stability.
Restrict only the painful wrist and ignore the neck
Bilateral hand symptoms may have a cervical source.
